title: Taking the 1934 band East, who would direct, and its size
summary: The band went East towards the Howard Theater with questions about who would direct the shows; it had five brass, four saxes and a rhythm section.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: We opened up, we got together -- where did we go? I think we went -- did we go South? No, we didn't go South. I think we went East. Yes, that's right. We went East. Uh-huh, we did. I think we went East with the band. And in that band, the boys was wondering who was going to direct the band, who was going to direct the shows, because they heard that we was going to play the Howard Theater and there was going to be a big show there, and they began to ask me, who's going to direct the show? Who's going to direct the band? Lord knows it was trouble.
Uh-huh. It was a younger band, a lot of young guys in the band?
Not too young. They wasn't too young, this time. No, they were around -- some of them were round about my age.
Uh-huh. Each succeeding band got larger.
Yes, that's right. Because each band was -- this was about the largest, excusing the band that he had at -- Louis Russell's band.
Yeah, yeah. Let's see, you had, again,
five brass -- did you have three or four saxes?
I had -- I'm trying to pinpoint in my mind who was the second tenor man that we had.
I think we did have four. I know --

Yes, because we had five brass, we had three trumpets -- five brass, six, with Louis, because when Louis come in, it would be four trumpets. Myself on the trumpet, and there was Milton Fletcher and this other fellow, I forget his name, yeah. Eddie Fantom on trombone, Judge George Dunlap on trombone, yeah.
